_doc: Platted street widths measured off the Hathaway 1834 sheet, street by street, to settle the disagreement recorded in data/traces/street_control.json: 80 ft annotated on this sheet against Currey's 66 ft for the 1830 plat. This is a measurement of the drawn corridors — block boundary line centre to block boundary line centre — and not a second reading of the annotation. Pixel positions are the evidence and are committed as such; metres are derived from them through the same fitted affine tools/rederive_datum.py checks the datum against, and check_street_module in tools/validate.py re-derives every one of them offline on every commit. Written by tools/measure_street_widths.py, which needs the network and is therefore not part of tools/check.sh.
confidence_note: The corridor width is measured off a cadastral survey sheet at a stated place with a stated method, reproducible by re-running the tool — which is what documented means here. What it is documented ABOUT is the sheet: the figure it supports is the width Hathaway draws, and the 3.7-4.5% anisotropic stretch of these sheets puts about a metre of local scale error on a 24 m street. That is small against the 4.27 m between the two candidate figures and large against the 0.6 m between 18 ft and 16 ft alleys, which is why the streets are settled here and the alleys are not.

method.anchors: each station stands on a committed control point in data/traces/street_control.json, offset along the street by station_m metres, so the sample sites are re-derivable from data
method.direction: the street's direction in raster space comes from two control points on it where two exist, and from a parallel street where only one does; each site records which
method.profile: ink fraction stepped along the street's normal, each sample averaged over a band_m run ALONG the street, because the plat grid sits off the raster axes and a column-wise profile smears a boundary line
method.line_test: a run of the profile is a block boundary only if inked over line_frac of the band; lot numerals, street names and the sheet's own width annotations sit in these corridors and cover a fraction of it
method.width: centre of the nearest qualifying line on one side to the centre of the nearest on the other, rejected unless the space between them reads as paper; centroids rather than edges, so the reading does not depend on how heavily either line was inked

summary.tolerance_note: The figure a reading supports is the candidate within tolerance_ft of the town median. 4 ft is the local scale error these sheets carry (3.7-4.5% of 80 ft is 3.0-3.6 ft) rounded up, and it is deliberately smaller than half the 14 ft between the candidates, so the band cannot admit both.
